newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian attorney-general quits - news agency.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian attorney-general quits - news agency.

text.p: Attorney-General Khaled al-Kidra has quit his job in President Yasser Arafat's Palestinian Authority, the official news agency WAFA said on Thursday.
The Palestinian agency said Arafat accepted Kidra's resignation on Wednesday night. Kidra was unavailable for comment, and the WAFA report did not provide a reason for his departure.

"President Yasser Arafat, head of the Palestine Liberation Organisation executive committee and head of the Palestinian National Authority, has approved a request by Attorney-General Mr Khaled al-Kidra to be relieved of his post," WAFA said.
Kidra, a lawyer in Gaza, was appointed attorney-general after Arafat returned home under a 1993 self-rule deal with Israel.
